hints: Look at the sign of $\Delta H^\ominus$ first, as this tells you whether products sit higher or lower in energy than reactants.
Remember $E_a$ is always measured upwards from the reactants level to the very top of the hump.
Check which diagram has products above reactants with both arrows starting correctly from the reactant energy level.
walkthrough:
**Decide endothermic or exothermic**

This is the key starting point. $\Delta H^\ominus = +90 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ is positive, so heat is absorbed.

$$\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{NO}(\text{g}) \quad \Delta H^\ominus = +90 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
This means the product $\text{NO(g)}$ must be higher in energy than the reactants.

**Recall what the arrows mean**

Think of the diagram like climbing over a hill. $E_a$ is the full climb from the reactants up to the peak. $\Delta H^\ominus$ is the overall change from reactants to products.

$$E_a = \text{energy(peak) - energy(reactants)}$$
$$\Delta H^\ominus = \text{energy(products) - energy(reactants)}$$

**Match to the diagrams**

Only diagrams B, C and D show products higher than reactants, so A is out as it shows an exothermic reaction. In B, the $E_a$ arrow starts at product level, not reactant level, and in D the $E_a$ arrow points downwards. Only one diagram shows products above reactants with $E_a$ drawn from reactants to the peak and $\Delta H^\ominus$ drawn from reactants to products.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows $\text{NO(g)}$ lower than $\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2 + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$, which is an exothermic profile with negative $\Delta H^\ominus$. Our reaction is endothermic with $+90 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so products must be higher.
options.B: Incorrect. The energy levels are correct for an endothermic reaction, but the $E_a$ arrow is wrong. It is drawn from the products level up to the peak. Activation energy must always be measured from the reactants level up to the peak.
options.C: Correct. Products $\text{NO(g)}$ are higher than reactants, matching positive $\Delta H^\ominus$. $E_a$ is correctly drawn from the reactant energy up to the top of the curve, and $\Delta H^\ominus$ is correctly drawn from reactants up to products.
options.D: Incorrect. Although products are correctly higher, the $E_a$ arrow is drawn pointing downwards from the peak to the reactants. By definition $E_a$ is the energy needed to go up from reactants to the transition state, so the arrow must point upwards.
